enzyme_name: unknown (no characterised enzyme condenses valienone 7-phosphate with validone 7-phosphate; the real C-N coupling step is run by the pseudoglycosyltransferase VldE/ValL)
organism_context: Streptomyces hygroscopicus subsp. jinggangensis (validamycin A producer)
rationale: Validoxylamine A's pseudo-glycosidic C-N bond is actually made by the OtsA-like pseudoglycosyltransferase VldE/ValL from GDP-valienol plus validamine 7-phosphate, not by condensing two C7-cyclitol ketones as this entry states, so no enzyme can be assigned to the reaction as written. (ValL is called bifunctional in a 2025 report because the same active site also makes a C-O-linked bis-valienol product, but that is substrate promiscuity of one glycosyl-transfer activity, not two fused catalytic domains.)
direction_note: Validoxylamine A is the committed pathway product so flux runs left-to-right, but the equation loses both 7-phosphates and invents the bridging nitrogen, which is why the group-contribution/dGPredictor numbers (~+500 kJ/mol) are meaningless here.

enzyme_name: methylecgonone reductase (MecgoR)
organism_context: Erythroxylum coca (Erythroxylaceae); an aldo-keto reductase, unrelated to the Solanaceae tropinone reductases
rationale: MecgoR is a single-domain NADPH-dependent aldo-keto reductase that stereospecifically reduces the 3-keto group of methylecgonone (2-carbomethoxy-3-tropinone) to methylecgonine in cocaine biosynthesis; only one catalytic activity is reported.
direction_note: NADPH has been replaced by a bare 2 H+, so every thermodynamic estimator scores the reduction as uphill and votes '<'; with the real hydride donor restored the enzyme runs only in the reduction direction the council chose.

enzyme_name: unknown (uncharacterised acyltransferase + epoxidase of the Pimpinella anisum pseudoisoeugenol pathway)
organism_context: Pimpinella anisum (anise) root/tissue culture; only PAL and cinnamate 4-hydroxylase of this pathway have been assayed
rationale: No protein has been purified or cloned for the esterification of pseudoisoeugenol with 2-methylbutyrate or for the subsequent epoxidation; MetaCyc PWY-5882 is built from feeding studies, so the catalyst is genuinely unknown.
direction_note: The entry collapses an acyl transfer (whose real donor is an activated 2-methylbutanoyl thioester) and an O2/NADPH-dependent epoxidation into one step; both are irreversible biosynthetic steps toward the epoxy ester, which is the direction the council picked.

enzyme_name: bacillibactin synthetase DhbF (glycine-activating adenylation domain)
organism_context: Bacillus subtilis dhb operon; DhbF is a two-module NRPS (C-A-PCP for Gly, C-A-PCP for Thr, plus a C-terminal TE)
rationale: The glycine adenylation step of bacillibactin assembly is run by an A domain embedded in the multidomain DhbF polypeptide, which also carries condensation and thioesterase catalytic domains on the same chain; the carrier (PCP) domains are not catalytic and were not counted.
direction_note: The adenylation half-reaction is near-isoenergetic in isolation, but in vivo it is pulled left-to-right by transfer of the aminoacyl group onto the PCP thiol and by pyrophosphatase, so the isolated ATP + Gly -> Gly-AMP + PPi entry should not be run in reverse.

enzyme_name: unknown (an NAD(P)H-dependent ene-reductase/C=C double-bond reductase)
organism_context: Monoterpene (carveol/dihydrocarveol) metabolism; in Rhodococcus erythropolis DCL14 the characterised route is carveol -> carvone -> dihydrocarvone -> dihydrocarveol, with no direct carveol reductase isolated
rationale: trans-Carveol and neo-dihydrocarveol differ by two hydrogens across the ring C=C, so the step requires an NAD(P)H ene-reductase, but no such enzyme acting directly on carveol has been purified; the best-characterised organism routes the same net change through carvone and dihydrocarvone with three separate enzymes.
direction_note: The hydride donor is missing and only 2 H+ is left, so thermodynamics reads it as an oxidation; biologically, NAD(P)H-driven alkene reduction is effectively one-way and the reverse (NAD+-dependent dehydrogenation of an unactivated C-C bond) does not occur.

enzyme_name: Pur4, putative 3'-keto-3'-deoxy-ATP aminotransferase of the puromycin pur cluster
organism_context: Streptomyces alboniger; assignment is from sequence similarity to aminotransferases within the deduced pur pathway (Pur10 makes the 3'-keto substrate)
rationale: Pur4 is a single-domain PLP aminotransferase homologue placed at this step by cluster analysis rather than by direct assay, and aminotransferases of this family carry only the transamination activity.
direction_note: The amino donor/acceptor pair (glutamate/2-oxoglutarate) has been dropped entirely, leaving an impossible keto-to-amine conversion; the pathway direction is unambiguously 3'-keto -> 3'-amino toward puromycin.

enzyme_name: unknown (no single enzyme; the N-methyl-L-glucosamine moiety is built from NDP-glucose by several str-cluster enzymes)
organism_context: Streptomyces griseus streptomycin pathway
rationale: Conversion of CDP/NDP-glucose to the N-methyl-L-glucosamine nucleotide requires at least a dehydratase/epimerase, a transaminase and an S-adenosylmethionine N-methyltransferase acting in sequence, so no one protein catalyses the entry as written.
direction_note: Flux in streptomycin biosynthesis runs from the sugar nucleotide to the N-methylaminosugar; the lumped entry also silently supplies an amine and a methyl group, so the computed deltaG is not interpretable.

enzyme_name: geosmin synthase (germacradienol/geosmin synthase, SCO6073/GeoA) - C-terminal cyclase domain
distinct_activities: germacradienol synthase: Mg2+-dependent ionisation/cyclisation of farnesyl diphosphate to (1(10)E,5E)-germacradien-11-ol + PPi (N-terminal class I terpenoid cyclase domain)
geosmin synthase: protonation-dependent cyclisation and retro-Prins fragmentation of germacradienol to geosmin + acetone (C-terminal domain)
organism_context: Streptomyces coelicolor A3(2); the alpha-alpha architecture is conserved in streptomycetes, myxobacteria and cyanobacteria
rationale: A single polypeptide carries two independent Mg2+-dependent class I terpenoid cyclase active sites: the N-terminal domain makes germacradienol from FPP and the C-terminal domain converts it to geosmin, which is the domain that performs the octalin cyclisation/hydration step in this entry.
direction_note: The C-terminal domain's protonation-initiated cyclisation and Markovnikov capture of water terminates the pathway at geosmin; the enzyme has no dehydratase activity, so the ModelSEED '<' (geosmin -> octalin + H2O) is backwards.

enzyme_name: norsolorinic acid anthrone synthase PksA (AflC/NorS), iterative non-reducing fungal polyketide synthase
organism_context: Aspergillus parasiticus / A. flavus aflatoxin cluster; all domains sit on one ~2100-residue chain
rationale: PksA is a single multidomain polypeptide whose SAT, KS, MAT, PT and TE/CLC domains each carry a distinct catalytic activity, demonstrated by domain dissection and the PT/TE crystal structures.
direction_note: The real reaction is hexanoyl-CoA + 7 malonyl-CoA -> norsolorinic acid anthrone + 7 CO2 + CoA; ModelSEED kept a single acetyl-CoA, so the ~600 kJ/mol estimates reflect the missing carbons, not the chemistry. Polyketide chain assembly with CO2 release is irreversible toward the anthrone.

enzyme_name: unknown (no single enzyme; versicolorin A -> 6-demethylsterigmatocystin needs AflN/VerA P450, AflM/Ver-1 NADPH reductase, AflX and AflY)
organism_context: Aspergillus parasiticus / A. flavus (stcS/stcU in A. nidulans)
rationale: KEGG itself annotates R10481 as a 'multi-step reaction' and assigns four separate orthologs (P450 monooxygenase, NADPH-dependent reductase, AflX, AflY) to it, so there is no single catalysing protein to classify; each of the four is individually a single-activity enzyme.
direction_note: The lumped sequence includes an irreversible P450 oxidation and a decarboxylative ring contraction, so it runs only versicolorin A -> demethylsterigmatocystin; KEGG's own 'multi-step' flag means the single deltaG is not a usable direction signal.

enzyme_name: unknown (the fructose-1,6-bisphosphate -> furanone step upstream of FaQR has no identified catalyst and may be non-enzymatic)
organism_context: Fragaria x ananassa (strawberry) furaneol pathway; the characterised enzyme FaQR acts on the next step (4-hydroxy-5-methyl-2-methylene-3(2H)-furanone -> HDMF), not on this one
rationale: Raab et al. established D-fructose-1,6-bisphosphate as the precursor and the methylene-furanone as FaQR's substrate, but no protein has been assigned to the sugar-to-furanone conversion itself, which is widely treated as spontaneous/uncharacterised.
direction_note: Two phosphates, water and a carbon are unaccounted for, which is why both estimators report ~+500 kJ/mol; the biological flux is sugar-phosphate -> furanone and is never reversed.

enzyme_name: unknown (UDP-glucose:HDMF glucosyltransferase plus a malonyl-CoA acyltransferase; neither cloned for this substrate)
organism_context: Fragaria x ananassa / Arabidopsis (MetaCyc, AraCyc PWY-5975)
rationale: The conjugate is formed by sequential UDP-glucose-dependent glucosylation of furaneol and malonyl-CoA-dependent 6'-O-malonylation; no purified enzyme is reported for either step on this aglycone, and the ModelSEED entry does not correspond to either half.
direction_note: Both donors (UDP-glucose and malonyl-CoA) and the malonyl group itself are absent from the equation, so left-to-right is impossible as literally written; the real enzymology is two irreversible group transfers that accumulate the malonylglucoside, which is the direction the council effectively chose.

enzyme_name: DmdA, DMSP/3-methylmercaptopropionate-dependent demethylase (methylthiopropanoate:tetrahydrofolate methyltransferase)
organism_context: Marine alphaproteobacteria - Pelagibacter ubique HTCC1062, Ruegeria (Silicibacter) pomeroyi DSS-3
rationale: DmdA is a single-domain glycine-cleavage T-protein (GcvT) family demethylase that transfers the S-methyl group of DMSP/MMPA onto tetrahydrofolate; only the methyltransfer activity has been demonstrated, and the downstream steps are carried by the separate DmdB/DmdC/DmdD proteins.
direction_note: The pathway exists to strip the methyl group off the thioether for carbon/C1 assimilation, so MMPA + THF -> 5-methyl-THF + 3-mercaptopropanoate is the physiological direction; the reverse (methylating a free thiol from methyl-THF) is not a DmdA activity.

enzyme_name: indole-3-acetate carboxyl methyltransferase (IAMT1), a SABATH-family SAM-dependent O-methyltransferase
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana; orthologues conserved across seed plants (Lotus japonicus LjIAMT1a/1b, rice, poplar)
rationale: IAMT1 is a small single-domain SABATH methyltransferase whose only reported activity is SAM-dependent methyl-esterification of IAA's carboxylate; the reverse hydrolysis is done by a separate methylesterase (MES17), not by IAMT1.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer with SAH release is effectively irreversible, and demethylation of MeIAA is catalysed by a distinct esterase, so ModelSEED's '<' assigns the wrong half of the interconversion to this enzyme.

enzyme_name: chlorobenzene cis-dihydrodiol dehydrogenase (cis-dihydrodiol dehydrogenase of the (di)chlorobenzene dioxygenase pathway; TcbB/CbzB-type)
organism_context: Xanthobacter flavus 14p1, Pseudomonas sp. P51, Pseudomonas putida GJ31, Pandoraea sp. MCB032
rationale: The dehydrogenase is a standalone NAD+-dependent short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase acting on the cis-dihydrodiol; the multicomponent character of this pathway belongs to the upstream dioxygenase (oxygenase/ferredoxin/reductase subunits), not to this single-activity enzyme.
direction_note: Rearomatisation of the cis-dihydrodiol to the catechol is strongly exergonic and physiologically one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would have NADH dearomatising a chlorocatechol, which no dehydrogenase does.

enzyme_name: RppA, 1,3,6,8-tetrahydroxynaphthalene synthase (bacterial type III polyketide synthase)
organism_context: Streptomyces griseus, S. coelicolor, Saccharopolyspora erythraea, Nocardia sp. CS682
rationale: RppA is a ~40 kDa chalcone-synthase-like homodimer with a single Cys-His-Asn active site that performs all five iterative decarboxylative condensations and the cyclisation in one pocket - one catalytic activity, not fused domains.
direction_note: Five malonyl-CoA condensations release four CO2, but the entry writes only one, which inflates the estimated deltaG; the decarboxylative Claisen chemistry makes the reaction irreversible toward tetrahydroxynaphthalene.

enzyme_name: NemA, N-ethylmaleimide reductase (FMN-containing Old Yellow Enzyme family NAD(P)H oxidoreductase)
organism_context: Escherichia coli (nemRA operon); homologues in Yarrowia lipolytica and Pseudomonas xenobiotic reductases
rationale: NemA is a single-domain FMN flavoprotein that transfers a hydride from NAD(P)H to the activated C=C of N-ethylmaleimide; its only catalytic activity is alkene reduction (the paired NemR is a separate regulator protein, not a fused domain).
direction_note: NAD(P)H has been replaced by bare protons, making the detoxifying reduction look thermodynamically uphill; with the flavin/NADH couple present the enzyme runs only toward N-ethylsuccinimide.

enzyme_name: LpxT (YeiU), undecaprenyl-pyrophosphate:lipid A 1-phosphate phosphotransferase
organism_context: Escherichia coli inner membrane, periplasmic active site; PAP2/type-2 phosphatase superfamily
rationale: LpxT is a single polytopic membrane protein with one phosphotransferase activity: it moves the distal phosphate of undecaprenyl pyrophosphate onto the 1-phosphate of lipid A, producing Und-P and lipid A 1-diphosphate.
direction_note: The reaction is driven by Und-PP hydrolysis and feeds the Und-P carrier-lipid recycling pool, so it is physiologically one-way; ModelSEED's '<' would have lipid A 1-diphosphate re-phosphorylating undecaprenyl phosphate, which is not observed.

enzyme_name: NAD(P)H:quinone oxidoreductase (two-electron quinone reductase of the WrbA/MdaB flavodoxin-like class)
organism_context: Escherichia coli and other bacteria (WrbA, MdaB); EC 1.6.5.- is unassigned in the MetaCyc entry, so the specific protein for methyl-1,4-benzoquinone is inferred from the class
rationale: WrbA/MdaB-type NQOs are single-domain FMN flavoproteins that catalyse only obligate two-electron transfer from NAD(P)H to a quinone; the family has no second catalytic activity. Protein identity for this specific quinone is inferred from the class, not confirmed.
direction_note: The whole point of these enzymes is to keep quinones reduced (avoiding one-electron semiquinone chemistry), so NADPH + quinone -> NADP+ + quinol is the only physiological direction; the eQuilibrator '<' reflects the awkward 4 H+ stoichiometry rather than the enzymology.

enzyme_name: nicotine N-demethylase - cytochrome P450 CYP2A6 (with a minor CYP2B6 contribution)
organism_context: Human liver (MetaCyc PWY66-201 is the human nicotine pathway); the plant counterpart is CYP82E4 in Nicotiana
rationale: Nornicotine formation from nicotine in human liver microsomes is catalysed by CYP2A6 and CYP2B6; each is a single-activity monooxygenase, and its obligatory partner NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase is a separate polypeptide (an electron-transfer pair, not a fused bifunctional enzyme).
direction_note: O2 and NADPH are both missing from the equation; P450 N-demethylation via a carbinolamine that collapses to formaldehyde is irreversible, so there is no chemistry behind ModelSEED's '<'.

enzyme_name: unknown (an unassigned NAD(P)H-dependent carbonyl reductase of human nicotine/NNK metabolism)
organism_context: Human (and rat/monkey) metabolism of nicotine and the tobacco-specific nitrosamine NNK; both the keto acid and the hydroxy acid are established urinary metabolites but no enzyme has been assigned to the interconversion
rationale: 4-Oxo-4-(3-pyridyl)butanoate is reduced to 4-hydroxy-4-(3-pyridyl)butanoate by cytosolic carbonyl-reducing activity that has never been resolved to a specific protein; candidate families (CBR1, AKR1C) are all single-activity carbonyl reductases.
direction_note: With NAD(P)H written out as 2 H+ the estimators see an impossible bare reduction and vote '<'; carbonyl reductases operating at cellular NADPH/NADP+ ratios run strongly toward the alcohol.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous ring-chain tautomerisation of a carbinolamine
organism_context: Human nicotine metabolism: CYP2A6 2'-hydroxylation of nicotine gives 2'-hydroxynicotine, whose open-chain tautomer is pseudooxynicotine (4-(methylamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone)
rationale: The two species are ring-closed and ring-opened tautomers of the same C10H14N2O carbinolamine and equilibrate non-enzymatically; the enzymatic step in this pathway is the preceding 2'-hydroxylation, not this interconversion.
direction_note: A spontaneous tautomeric equilibrium has no enzyme to set its direction - net flux is simply toward whichever tautomer is drained (here pseudooxynicotine, consumed onward to the keto acid), so neither a fixed '<' nor a fixed '>' is defensible.

enzyme_name: 11beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 1 (11beta-HSD1)
organism_context: Human liver microsomes (ER lumen); human activity is ~10x rat and ~80x mouse
rationale: Recombinant 11beta-HSD1 was shown to be the major enzyme forming threohydrobupropion, and it is a single-domain SDR carbonyl oxidoreductase - running the same reaction in both directions is one catalytic activity, and its NADPH-regenerating partner H6PD is a separate protein.
direction_note: NADPH is absent from the equation; inside the ER lumen H6PD keeps 11beta-HSD1 in reductase mode, so bupropion -> threohydrobupropion is the direction that actually runs.

enzyme_name: cytosolic carbonyl reductases - CBR1 and AKR1C1/AKR1C2/AKR1C3 (AKR7 in intestine)
organism_context: Human liver cytosol/mitochondria and intestine
rationale: Erythrohydrobupropion is formed by carbonyl reductases other than 11beta-HSD1 - CBR1 and the AKR1C isoforms were directly demonstrated - and each is a single-active-site NADPH carbonyl reductase (the AKR1C enzymes' several hydroxysteroid 'activities' are the same reduction chemistry at different positions, not fused domains).
direction_note: Same defect as the threo isomer: NADPH written as 2 H+ makes the reduction look uphill, while the real cytosolic NADPH pool drives bupropion -> erythrohydrobupropion.

enzyme_name: SULT1A3, monoamine (catecholamine) sulfotransferase
organism_context: Human cytosol (gut, platelets, liver); explains the predominance of dopamine-3-O-sulfate in circulation
rationale: SULT1A3 is a single-domain cytosolic sulfotransferase whose only activity is PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer; it sulfonates dopamine regioselectively at the 3-O position.
direction_note: PAPS-dependent sulfuryl transfer is a high-energy group transfer pulled strongly toward the sulfoconjugate plus PAP; desulfation in vivo is done by separate sulfatases, so the '<' assignment is not this enzyme's reaction.
